burdens.eyebrow: Where a finance Work Agent earns its place
burdens.title: Spend analyst time on interpretation, not rebuilding the evidence trail.
burdens.description: Financial analysis breaks down when updated numbers, operating explanations, model assumptions, and management commentary no longer reconcile to the same period and source.

items.label: Context
items.title: Numbers and narrative live apart
items.description: A workbook may show the movement while filings, transcripts, emails, and operating notes contain the explanation.

items.label: Format
items.title: Source updates trigger repetitive work
items.description: Each new filing, forecast, close, or market update triggers another round of extraction, normalization, and commentary.

items.label: Coordination
items.title: Assumptions disappear inside models
items.description: Inputs change across tabs and versions, while the reason, owner, date, and downstream effect of the change are easy to lose.

items.label: Continuity
items.title: Recurring reports restart from old copies
items.description: Monthly and weekly reviews are often rebuilt from copied files instead of a controlled trail of sources, assumptions, and changes.

buildingBlocks.eyebrow: What your finance Work Agent can prepare
buildingBlocks.title: Turn approved figures and context into review-ready analysis materials.
buildingBlocks.description: The Work Agent uses its workspace to connect source documents, periods, units, assumptions, and drafts while analysts retain every financial conclusion.

items.example: Read approved statements, filings, transcripts, operating notes, and metric definitions for the same period.
Tag each figure with source, period, currency, unit, and calculation status.
Extract reported metrics, management explanations, assumption changes, and unresolved questions.
Compare actuals with plan and prior periods without silently mixing units or definitions.
Draft a company brief, driver commentary, and questions tied to source figures.
items.result: Editable analysis materials, not a recommendation.

items.example: Reuse the approved metric map, reconciliation checks, and sign-off points at the next close.

workflows.eyebrow: Three assignments for a finance Work Agent
workflows.title: Delegate evidence preparation without delegating financial judgment.
workflows.description: Each assignment starts from approved sources and definitions, returns traceable work, and stops before materiality, valuation, forecast, or investment decisions.

items.title: Prepare a company research packet
items.job: Organize filings, transcripts, metrics, and open questions before deeper analysis.
items.output: A source-linked company brief and diligence question list.
items.boundary: Analysts verify every figure and decide what is financially material.

items.title: Draft a variance review
items.job: Connect actuals, plan, prior periods, and operating context into an editable management narrative.
items.output: A variance table, drivers, and review-ready commentary.
items.boundary: Finance owners validate calculations, causes, and management implications.

items.title: Maintain recurring market monitoring
items.job: Update a controlled watchlist and surface changes that deserve analyst attention.
items.output: A dated monitoring brief with changed assumptions and follow-ups.
items.boundary: The analyst decides significance and retains all investment or financial judgment.

customization.title: Teach the Work Agent your finance definitions and review rules.
customization.description: Provide periods, currencies, units, metric definitions, assumption registers, templates, and approval points before it prepares the deliverable.

progression.eyebrow: From one assignment to a reusable Work Agent
progression.title: Validate one closed period before reusing the Work Agent routine.
progression.description: Reuse should follow a completed reconciliation, not precede it; every new period still requires source, unit, and assumption checks.

items.label: Ad hoc
items.title: Rebuild one signed-off variance review
items.description: Use approved actuals, plan, metric definitions, and operating notes to reproduce one prior-period table and commentary for comparison.

items.label: Saved workflow
items.title: Carry the controls into the next period
items.description: Reuse the period mapping, unit checks, assumption register, commentary format, and analyst sign-off—not the prior conclusions.

items.label: Team practice
items.title: Standardize the review pack
items.description: Let finance owners begin from the same sourced tables and review questions while each owner validates their figures and explanations.

boundaries.title: Let the Work Agent prepare the record. Keep every financial conclusion accountable.
boundaries.description: The Work Agent can assemble and compare approved financial evidence; it cannot certify calculations, decide materiality, set a forecast, or make an investment recommendation.

boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Work Agent, not a financial model, ERP, market-data terminal, or investment adviser. Its workspace keeps approved sources, instructions, tools, and deliverables connected; analysts remain responsible for calculations and conclusions.

faq.title: Work Agent questions for financial analysts and finance teams
faq.description: Finance teams need number-level provenance, visible assumptions, period consistency, and clear ownership of every financial conclusion.

items.question: Is Floatboat a financial model, ERP, or market-data terminal?
items.answer: No. Those systems remain the sources of record and calculation. Floatboat helps analysts organize approved extracts, filings, transcripts, assumptions, and commentary into reviewable work products.

items.question: Can it make an investment or financial recommendation?
items.answer: It can prepare evidence, changes, scenarios, and questions, but analysts remain responsible for materiality, valuation, forecasts, recommendations, and any decision based on them.

items.question: Can it follow our chart of accounts, KPI definitions, or research template?
items.answer: Yes. Supply the approved metric definitions, periods, sign conventions, reporting structure, assumption register, and review format before analysis begins.

items.question: How do we keep numbers from being mixed across periods or units?
items.answer: Carry source, period, currency, unit, and calculation status with each figure; reject silent gaps; and reconcile all numbers to the source system or approved model before using the commentary.

items.question: How should confidential financial data be handled?
items.answer: Use only data permitted by company policy and applicable obligations, restrict each workspace to necessary files, and review the processing and retention behavior of every model and connector.

items.question: Will it publish a report or update a model automatically?
items.answer: Not in the recommended workflow. Draft commentary, watchlist updates, and proposed changes remain pending until an analyst validates the figures and approves the destination.

items.question: What is a practical first finance workflow?
items.answer: Take one completed reporting period, provide the approved actuals, plan, definitions, and operating notes, then compare the generated variance table and commentary with the signed-off version.

finalCta.title: Give your first financial-preparation assignment to a Work Agent.
finalCta.description: Start with one closed period or one researched company. Keep every figure tied to its source, unit, date, and assumption before reusing the workflow.
